title: Miso-Sesame Tofu & Broccoli Bowls
dek: Crisp tofu, broccoli, corn, cucumber, and carrots with a savory-sweet miso sesame dressing.
image_alt: Tofu broccoli corn and vegetable bowl with sesame dressing
ingredients: 14 oz extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed

instructions.name: Crisp the tofu
instructions.text: Toss pressed tofu with cornstarch and oil. Bake at 425°F for 20 to 22 minutes, turning once.

instructions.name: Roast the broccoli
instructions.text: Add broccoli to a second pan or alongside tofu for the final 14 minutes, lightly oiled and salted.

instructions.name: Whisk the dressing
instructions.text: Mix miso, soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, sesame oil, ginger, and 2 tablespoons warm water.

instructions.name: Prep the toppings
instructions.text: Warm corn and chop cucumber and carrot.

instructions.name: Build
instructions.text: Layer rice, tofu, broccoli, corn, cucumber, and carrot. Drizzle generously with miso dressing and sesame seeds.

why_it_works: Cornstarch gives baked tofu a crisp shell.
Miso dressing supplies enough umami that the bowl does not miss meat.
Hot roasted vegetables and cool cucumber create contrast.
storage: Refrigerate tofu, rice, and broccoli up to 4 days. Store dressing separately.
notes: Press tofu at least 15 minutes for better browning.
Thin dressing with warm water, not extra oil, so it stays punchy.

faqs.q: Can I air fry the tofu?
faqs.a: Yes. Air fry at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking twice.
Use tamari and verify your miso is gluten-free.
Yes, roast from frozen and allow a few extra minutes.

title: Cajun Crispy Chicken & Pepper Pasta
dek: Crispy chicken cutlets over creamy Cajun pasta with peppers, onions, and Parmesan.
image_alt: Sliced seasoned chicken served over creamy pasta

instructions.name: Bread the chicken
instructions.text: Season chicken with 1 tablespoon Cajun seasoning. Dredge in flour, egg, then panko.

instructions.name: Crisp
instructions.text: Shallow-fry chicken in oil over medium-high until golden and 165°F, about 3 to 4 minutes per side. Rest on a rack.

instructions.name: Cook pasta
instructions.text: Boil linguine until al dente and reserve 1 cup pasta water.

instructions.name: Build the sauce
instructions.text: Sauté peppers and onion until crisp-tender. Add garlic and remaining Cajun seasoning, then broth and cream. Simmer 3 minutes.

instructions.name: Finish
instructions.text: Toss pasta with Parmesan and enough pasta water to coat. Slice chicken over top and finish with scallions.

why_it_works: A rack keeps the chicken crust crisp while the sauce finishes.
Cajun seasoning is split between chicken and sauce for layered flavor.
Peppers stay slightly firm so the pasta has texture.
swaps: Use smoked paprika plus oregano if you do not have Cajun seasoning.
storage: Refrigerate chicken and pasta separately up to 3 days. Re-crisp chicken in an air fryer or oven.
notes: Taste Cajun seasoning before adding extra salt.
Do not put fried chicken directly into the sauce or the crust will soften.

faqs.q: Can I air fry the chicken?
faqs.a: Yes. Spray well and air fry at 390°F until crisp and cooked through.
Usually medium. Cajun blends vary, so adjust to your brand.

title: Thai Chili Turkey Meatball Noodle Bowls
dek: Tender turkey meatballs, rice noodles, herbs, and vegetables in a sweet-spicy chile-lime sauce.
image_alt: Meatball noodle bowl with herbs and chili sauce

instructions.name: Shape the meatballs
instructions.text: Mix turkey, egg, panko, scallions, ginger, garlic, and soy sauce. Form about 20 small meatballs.

instructions.name: Cook
instructions.text: Bake at 425°F for 12 to 15 minutes until browned and 165°F.

instructions.name: Cook noodles
instructions.text: Prepare rice noodles according to package directions, rinse briefly, and drain well.

instructions.name: Make the sauce
instructions.text: Whisk sweet chili sauce, lime juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and 2 tablespoons water.

instructions.name: Build
instructions.text: Toss noodles with half the sauce. Add meatballs, pepper, cucumber, herbs, remaining sauce, and peanuts.

why_it_works: Small turkey meatballs stay tender because they cook quickly.
Rice vinegar and lime sharpen the sweet chile sauce.
Fresh herbs make the bowl taste lighter than a typical noodle takeout dish.
swaps: Use soba noodles instead of rice noodles.
storage: Refrigerate meatballs and noodles up to 4 days. Store herbs and sauce separately.
notes: Do not compress the meat mixture while shaping.
Rinse rice noodles only briefly so they do not become cold and waterlogged.

faqs.q: Can I make the meatballs ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Shape them up to a day ahead or freeze raw meatballs on a tray.
It is mild to medium. Add sambal or sriracha for more heat.
Yes. It works well as a chilled noodle bowl.

title: Coconut Curry Tofu Ramen
dek: Golden tofu and ramen noodles in a creamy red-curry coconut broth with greens and lime.
image_alt: Tofu ramen in spicy coconut curry broth
ingredients: 14 oz extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed
8 oz ramen noodles, seasoning packets discarded
2 cups baby bok choy or spinach

instructions.name: Brown the tofu
instructions.text: Sear tofu in oil in a Dutch oven until golden on several sides. Transfer out.

instructions.name: Bloom the curry
instructions.text: Add curry paste, ginger, and garlic to the pot. Cook 45 seconds.

instructions.name: Build the broth
instructions.text: Add vegetable broth, coconut milk, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Simmer 8 minutes.

instructions.name: Cook noodles
instructions.text: Add ramen noodles and greens. Cook just until noodles are tender.

instructions.name: Finish
instructions.text: Return tofu, add lime juice, and serve with scallions, cilantro, and chili oil.

why_it_works: Browning tofu first gives it a chewy edge that survives the broth.
Curry paste is fried briefly to deepen its aromatics.
Lime at the end keeps coconut broth from tasting flat.
swaps: Add mushrooms with the curry paste.
Use chicken broth if the dish does not need to stay vegan.
storage: Broth and tofu keep 4 days. Store noodles separately when meal-prepping so they do not absorb all the liquid.
notes: Curry pastes vary in salt and heat; season after simmering.
Do not overcook ramen noodles—they soften quickly in hot broth.

faqs.q: Can I use light coconut milk?
faqs.a: Yes, but the broth will be thinner.
A jammy egg is excellent if you do not need the recipe to stay vegan.
